plans.note: Primary text is sec-21 (LIMITATION OF LIABILITY). Check mutuality of the cap, the multiplier/fees-paid measure, exclusion of indirect damages, and whether the 'Excluded Claims' definition in sec-1 carves out IP indemnity, confidentiality, data breach and willful misconduct. Cross-check sec-20 for uncapped indemnity language.

sec-20 should contain Vendor's third-party IP infringement and misconduct indemnities plus defence/control mechanics; confirm any Customer-side indemnity is narrow (Customer Data / breach of use restrictions only) and that indemnity sits outside the sec-21 cap via 'Excluded Claims'.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline; if present it would be buried in CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES (sec-12) or GENERAL (sec-30). Scan for any restriction on competing products or building similar functionality before concluding absent.

Check the scope language in sec-2 and the Order Form/Affiliate Order mechanics in sec-4 for 'sole and exclusive provider' or 'all requirements' wording; otherwise treat as absent (no rule requires an exclusivity clause to exist).

Direction rule: look in FEES (sec-7) and GENERAL (sec-30) for any 'best terms'/'most favoured' language. Only flag if it obliges Customer to extend best terms to Vendor; an MFN in our favour is welcome and must not be redlined.

Typically sits in GENERAL (sec-30) or alongside confidentiality (sec-16). If found, test duration (≤12 months), limitation to personnel actually engaged on the Services, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out.

sec-9 (TERMINATION) is the anchor: confirm Customer may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice without early-termination fees, and that Vendor has no symmetric convenience right mid-term. Check sec-10 for penalty-style consequences that undercut the exit.

sec-8 (TERM AND RENEWAL) — assess auto-renewal length, the non-renewal notice window (prefer ≤30 days, resist 90+), and any renewal price uplift. A missing uplift cap or renewal reminder is a rationale note, not a standalone deviation.

sec-28 (GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION). Check the chosen law against NY/DE/CA/England and Wales and whether disputes go to courts rather than foreign-seated arbitration; an accepted-but-not-preferred law is noted only.

sec-24 (ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL) — confirm Customer may assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger/asset sale without consent, and that Vendor has no termination right triggered by our change of control. Check sec-30 for a residual assignment clause.

sec-14 governs Deliverables ownership; sec-15 governs Customer Data. Confirm Customer owns paid-for Deliverables and all Customer Data, that any Vendor Technology licence-back is limited, and that no clause assigns our IP or data (including feedback or derived/aggregated data) to Vendor.

sec-13 (ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE) — test whether the grant extends to Affiliates and contractors/service providers acting for us, and whether it is stated as revocable at will or otherwise suspendable outside a breach process.

sec-22 (AUDIT RIGHTS) is likely Vendor-side audit of our usage: check frequency (≤1/year), advance written notice, business-hours/off-site-where-possible, confidentiality, and that Vendor bears cost absent material underpayment. sec-23 may hold our reciprocal assurance rights — do not flag rights that benefit us.

Direction rule: service credits or SLA remedies running to us (likely sec-3) are welcome and must not be flagged. Look in sec-7 for late-payment interest/penalties and in sec-9/sec-10 for early-termination or shortfall charges payable by Customer.

sec-19 (WARRANTIES) — assess the performance/conformity warranty, its duration, and whether the remedy is meaningful (re-performance plus refund) rather than sole-and-exclusive repair only. Cross-reference acceptance testing in sec-6 and service levels in sec-3, and check for a broad disclaimer of implied warranties.

sec-18 (INSURANCE) exists; verify it covers commercial general liability, professional liability/E&O and cyber given Vendor hosts Customer Data, with adequate limits and evidence-of-coverage obligations.

Check Order Form mechanics (sec-4) and Fees (sec-7) for committed volumes, take-or-pay, non-reducible seat counts or ratchets on renewal; if a commitment exists, confirm an exit or true-down path exists via sec-8/sec-9.

sec-11 (TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN) is on point: confirm a defined assistance period, data return in a usable format at reasonable or no cost, and that sec-10's deletion/effect-of-termination provisions do not allow deletion before we have retrieved our Customer Data.
